findings.claim: In the default (no SurrogateType) path, `Collect` always calls `CreateContractlessMembers`. That path ignores every MessagePack attribute on `T`: `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key]`, `[IgnoreMember]` and `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]` are never read. A `T` with `[IgnoreMember] public string Secret { get; set; }` therefore still has `Secret` serialized. Members marked `[Key(0)]` or `[Key("v")]` are written under their member names as string keys instead of the declared keys. This breaks the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured.' The output is also not byte-compatible with the formatter the defining assembly's own resolver produces.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptsTests.IgnoreMemberOnReferencedTypeIsHonoured. A referenced ProjectA type has [MessagePackObject] with an [IgnoreMember] property `Secret`. The test asserts that the formatter generated for it in ProjectB does not mention `Secret`. On head the contractless path emits `value.Secret`, so the test fails.

findings.claim: `needsCast` compares `m.Name` with "OnBeforeSerialize"/"OnAfterDeserialize" only for methods that have ExplicitInterfaceImplementations. An explicit implementation's Name is the qualified "MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize", so the check never matches. It also inspects only `type.GetMembers()`, not base types, and private explicit impls are not imported from metadata. As a result, any `T` that implements IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver explicitly gets `needsCast = false`. The template then emits `value.OnBeforeSerialize()`, which fails to compile (CS1061) in the generated code.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptsTests.ExplicitCallbackReceiverCompiles. It runs the generator over a type that explicitly implements IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver and has a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] formatter for it. It then asserts the updated compilation has no errors. On head this fails with CS1061 in the generated formatter.

findings.claim: `IsPartial` checks only the formatter's own declaration. Containing types are not checked. A formatter nested in a non-partial class (`class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> { } }`) passes validation, and the template then emits `partial class F` inside the nesting from EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces. If that nesting reproduces Outer, the output fails with CS0260 (missing partial on Outer) instead of an MsgPack019/MsgPack011-style diagnostic. A private nested formatter is also accepted even though the generated resolver must instantiate it.

receipt_plan.detail: IsPartial (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs, end of file) inspects only the ClassDeclarationSyntax of `formatter`. No check walks formatter.ContainingType for the partial modifier or for accessibility from the resolver. Confirm by generating for a formatter nested in a non-partial class and compiling the output.

findings.claim: Each [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] model is added to `modelPerType` unconditionally. If `T` is also a [MessagePackObject] type in the same compilation, or two generated formatters target the same `T`, two ObjectSerializationInfos for the same data type reach the resolver. Depending on the resolver template and the ObjectInfos comparer, this either drops one formatter silently (sorted-set dedupe) or registers `typeof(T)` twice in the resolver lookup, which throws at type initialization. No diagnostic is reported for the duplicate.

receipt_plan.detail: MessagePackGenerator.cs:70-76 adds the generated model without checking for an existing ObjectInfo with the same DataType. Generate for a source type that has [MessagePackObject] together with a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class for that same type, then inspect the generated resolver.
